correctness.rationale: Every simplex fixed by a nonidentity translation must be a union of two-point translation orbits. A cube closed neighborhood contains no orbit when \(\operatorname{wt}(a)>2\), and exactly one orbit when \(\operatorname{wt}(a)=1\) or \(2\). Thus the only invariant faces are \(2^{n-1}\) orientation-reversing edges in the latter cases. The Hopf trace formula and Adams--Shukla--Singh Theorem 4.1 give the complete \(H_2\) character, while rational Fourier inversion yields \(m_{n,0}=\binom n2\) and \(m_{n,k}=\binom n2+1-k(n+1-k)\) for \(k>0\). The checker exhausts signed traces for \(2\le n\le7\), mod-two chain ranks for \(2\le n\le5\), and multiplicity sums for \(2\le n\le13\). Published homological concentration is an explicit premise; finite tests are not treated as an infinite proof.
